purpose: The page where a person changes how their account behaves for them. It is an organism-of-organisms: a page-header lock-up, a column of SECTIONED form groups each on its own card surface, a rail carrying in-page navigation and the save state, and an action bar that stays reachable. It contributes page-scale LAYOUT, section RHYTHM and the setting-row relationship - every control inside it is a gated component, borrowed.

Layer-2 rows have no ruled artefact form; this file ships in the library's grammar on the brief's PROPOSED convention (s182-D2, the Kpi-tile precedent). No registration was performed: no CATEGORIES entry, no MIGRATED_SNIPPETS entry, no component-types.json membership, no canon.css block, no _rulings.json line, no gen_kg_edges.py run, no git operation. Deleting this pair costs nothing because nothing points at it.
$layer-note: The wave-5 and wave-6 briefs PROPOSED the meta key `layer`. meta.schema.json is additionalProperties:false with patternProperties '^\\$' only, so a bare `layer` key FAILS probe P-1 (probe_meta_schema.py). `$layer` is the legal form and is what is used here - the correction #210 wave-5 lane C reported, carried forward, not re-discovered. A `$`-prefixed key is an ANNOTATION by the schema's own grammar: if Layer-2 membership is meant to be queryable structure it wants a real enum property and a schema amendment. Still open, still Dave's.

props.name: sections
props.$note: Four are drawn: text fields, switches, a radio group plus a segmented control, and checkboxes plus a segmented control. Each is a <fieldset> on a Stat-card surface.

props.name: rail
props.$note: The in-page jump list and the save-state panel. Present it is a 280px rail; absent the form column takes the full width. The rail moves BELOW the form when the split's CONTAINER is <=760px.

props.name: stickyActions
props.$note: The action bar is position:sticky against the nearest SCROLLPORT. On a real page that is the page. See the antiPattern.

variants.name: clean
variants.use: No unsaved changes. The rail's chip is absent and the action bar's primary is the resting state.

variants.name: dirty
variants.use: Unsaved changes exist. Drawn: the rail carries an information chip reading 'Two changes not yet saved'. Ink on a tint, never a warning seat - see the antiPattern.

variants.name: field error
variants.use: A setting fails a rule. Drawn on the Security section: Selection-controls' error ATOM (s151-D1 clause 3 - the atom takes the red, the label keeps default ink) plus an .err-msg carrying a symbol AND a sentence.

tokens.divider: divider/border/section - the page's own section rules
tokens.focus: focus/ring - read only by the demo bar
tokens.$parts: Every other colour, radius, size and face on the page belongs to a part and is bound in THAT part's #token-manifest; the page binds nothing for them (s307-D75: the rules live in the shared stylesheet, not on the page).
tokens.$mono: MONO base rendered; the other themes reach the page through canon.css's theme cascade on each part's scope.
tokens.$noNewWidths: s210-D3 discipline: the template asserts page-scale layout only. No molecule inside it receives a new fixed width.

$composes-note: REBUILT #314 lane TP (s313-D72, Dave's comment verbatim: "We need to regenerate the templates too BTW, everything in the library should be a valid 'element' of the design system"). The template is a composed PAGE: its snippet links canon/canon.css and places each part above as its own .cn-<slug> scope with the part's own markup; the page's <style> carries placement rules only (s305-D57 rule 3a; s307-D75). Before #314 it carried copies of the parts' rules and canon.css projected that second copy under its own scope. The #210 prose that stood here (which classes were copied, declaration for declaration) is retired with the copies. FIX ROUND #314 TP: Discard changes is a quaternary Button in the Action-bar's slot (the bar lays actions out, never authors them); Reset to defaults is quaternary; email and mobile share Form-layout's own .fl-row; the lede is page prose under the lock-up.

accessibility.roles: No invented roles. Each section is a <section> holding a <fieldset> with a real <legend>; the rail is an <aside>; the jump list is a <nav>; the field error is role="alert".
accessibility.keyboard: Tab order follows source order: breadcrumb, page action, form sections top to bottom, rail, action bar. Every switch, radio and checkbox is a real native input driving state and announcement; the (?) help control is a real <button> with an accessible name.
accessibility.announcements: The field-level error message is role="alert". The save-state chip is a passive chip, not a live region - a settings page is a STATE, not a stream of events.
accessibility.states: aria-pressed on every segmented control; role="switch" on the notification toggles; the locked field carries the real disabled attribute so AT reports it, and the REASON sits in its help text rather than only in the visual dimming.
accessibility.targets: ⚠ MEASURED ON THE #210 BUILD, before the #314 rebuild as a composed page; not re-measured at #314. Every action-bar button is 44px tall. Every selection control's <label> is 44px tall - MEASURED at 44x44 for the bare switches and 44px tall for the text labels. Segment buttons are 32px (md) and 28px (sm) VISIBLE and carry Segmented-control's invisible >=44px ::before target. The (?) help control is 18px visible with the canon aid-009 ::before expander to 44.
accessibility.$colourIsNeverAlone: The error channel is a red ATOM plus a symbol plus a sentence in default ink (1.4.1). The save-state chip carries its word; the dot is aria-hidden.
accessibility.$knownDelta: Form-layout bumps an errored or completed input to font-weight:500 and Selection-controls sets its labels at 500. Both are raw font declarations, both are ABSENT here, because the canon ramp has no 16/500 INPUT or LABEL composite and a raw declaration would breach the shrink-only type ratchet. The error channel is unharmed but the WEIGHT cue is gone. Named for Dave, not smoothed over.
accessibility.$measuredDefect: ⚠ MEASURED ON THE #210 BUILD, before the #314 rebuild as a composed page; not re-measured at #314. The type ratchet ALSO clipped every field's descenders: .t-cm-input is 16px at line-height 1, an <input> clips to its own box, and the canon leading-trim :is() list includes input[type=text|email|tel]. MEASURED 9px clipped on the email field, VISIBLE in a 4x crop, and PASSED by _validate_descender_clip.py (a textual gate). Repaired with ds-005's TWO-CLASS form and re-measured to 0px with the computed text-box-edge reading `text`.

antiPatterns: Re-drawing a control. Every switch, radio, checkbox, segment and field on this page is a gated component's anatomy with its class names intact. If the language needs to change, change it at the source and let this page follow - never fork it here.

Putting a Segmented control in a `1fr auto` setting row without a container query. MEASURED at 420px: the explanation column crushed to 151px while the control kept 163px. This is the crushed-shrinkable-child class, n=3 across #209 and #210.

Assuming position:sticky sticks to the template. It sticks to the nearest SCROLLPORT. If a template is not the page, give it a scrollport - and measure the non-overlap AT THE SCROLL END, not at the initial scroll position, because a sticky bar is SUPPOSED to pass over content mid-scroll.
Treating a locked field as merely dimmed. A field the user may not change must say WHY in its help text.
REVIEW Adding a RAG hue to the unsaved-changes chip beyond rag/information. Whether an unsaved state is a WARNING is Dave's and touches the two-red law.
Declaring container-type on the element you then try to query. An element is a query container for its DESCENDANTS and never for itself; the rule silently never fires and the screenshot looks fine.

Copying a part's rules onto the page. The page places parts (its own .cn-<slug> scope + the part's own markup) and never resizes or restyles them (s305-D57 rule 3a, s307-D75). A template that re-declares a Button ladder, a Summary row or a Data-grid toolbar forks the part the moment the part moves.
